title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and deconfined criticality in SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$
abstract: SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ is the leading candidate for deconfined criticality, yet theories of its critical regime omit the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions, which gap the kagome Dirac spin liquid. Adding them to the SU(2) gauge theory, we show that time reversal and a spin-orbit-locked glide forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass to all orders. In-plane DM only twists the spinons, reconstructing the nodes below $0.03$-$0.17$ K, while out-of-plane DM is irrelevant and SO(5) anisotropy arises only at second order. The material thus remains a platform for deconfined criticality, which NMR can test, since a $[100]$ field induces a Néel moment and a $[001]$ field does not.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the role of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in the quantum magnet $	ext{SrCu}_2(	ext{BO}_3)_2$, a key candidate for deconfined criticality. Using gauge theory and symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate that these interactions do not gap the spinon continuum, confirming the material's status as a platform for exotic quantum phases. The work provides detailed predictions regarding the nature of the resulting quantum ground state.
main_problem: The study investigates the role of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions in determining the nature of deconfined criticality in the quantum magnet $	ext{SrCu}_2(	ext{BO}_3)_2$. The core question is whether these interactions gap the system's spinon continuum.
main_result: The symmetry analysis shows that time reversal and lattice symmetries forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass, meaning the system remains a platform for deconfined criticality. In-plane DM couplings reconstruct the Dirac nodes into a quadratic band touching, while out-of-plane couplings are irrelevant at low orders.
method: The analysis employs advanced theoretical techniques, including $	ext{SU}(2)$ gauge theory, renormalization group (RG) analysis, and detailed classification of fermion bilinears under specific symmetry groups ($\mathcal{T}$ and glide operations).
model_or_system: The system is the $	ext{SrCu}_2(	ext{BO}_3)_2$ antiferromagnet, modeled using an $	ext{SU}(2)$ gauge theory framework that incorporates Heisenberg exchange and DM couplings. The theoretical machinery analyzes emergent $	ext{SO}(5)$ symmetry.
key_observables: Gauge-singlet fermion masses (Néel, VBS, chirality), spinon Dirac cones, and the magnetic field dependence of the staggered moment ($\mathbf{N}$ vs $\mathbf{B}$).
important_parameters: Critical temperature scale $T^* \simeq 0.03-0.17$ K; the relevance of DM coupling strengths ($\lambda$); and the symmetry constraints imposed by $\mathcal{T}$ and lattice operations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the $	ext{SU}(2)$ gauge theory description and relies heavily on symmetry constraints derived from the spin-orbit-locked symmetry group.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the effect of DM on spinon Dirac cones, showing the reconstruction into a quadratic band touching. Tables summarize the action of symmetries on various fermion bilinears, confirming which order parameters are forbidden or induced.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the theoretical framework using gauge theory and symmetry analysis. It systematically classifies symmetry-allowed order parameters, analyzes the effect of in-plane versus out-of-plane DM couplings, and concludes by confirming the persistence of the deconfined critical state.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of how specific microscopic interactions (DM) interact with underlying symmetries to stabilize exotic quantum phases, which is crucial for understanding strongly correlated materials relevant to quantum simulation.
